subject: MAP: unit economics sensitivity + prefetch & batching ops runbook
messages:

Subject: MAP kickoff - unit-econ sensitivity + prefetch/batching Qs

Hi Lukas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prep the Mutual Action Plan I want to make sure we include an explicit evaluation axis for unit economics — specifically how tokens/$ change under different prefetching and batching strategies. A few quick asks so we can align internally and share with procurement: 

- Can you outline the baseline tokens-per-session and tokens-per-user assumptions you use for pilots?
- What prefetch/cache hit ratios do you typically model, and how does that change tokens/$ in your simulations?
- For batching: what latency vs. batch-size tradeoffs should we expect for 95th/99th pct SLOs?

We can share a small sample of traffic (attached) with timestamps/session ids if that helps. Procurement will want a conservative and a best-case units/$ number for the MAP (they escalate if there's >20% uncertainty).

Attached: Medicorps_prod_traffic_snapshot.csv (sample, 48h)

Goal: we want the MAP to include a definitive gating criterion on cost that both teams sign off on before pilot procurement. Can you propose owners/dates for those checkpoints?

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product, Medicorps
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - unit-econ sensitivity + prefetch/batching Qs

Samir — thanks for the clear asks and the traffic sample. High-level response and a proposed MAP runbook below. I attached a draft MAP workbook with scenarios (lukas_map_draft_v1.xlsx) and a short sim readout (inference-sim-results.pdf).

Summary / proposed scope for the MAP cost axis:
- Baseline tokens/session: we’ll run sims using your sample and two canonical profiles: 250 tokens/session (conservative) and 850 tokens/session (engaged users).
- Cache/prefetch modeling: we’ll evaluate two policies — prefix prefetch (warm KV cache on session start) and passive caching (no pre-warm). We simulate hit ratios at 30%, 60%, 85%.
- Batching assumptions: three operating points — <2ms per-token extra for batch size 1 (no batching), batch size target 8 (amortized kernel overhead reduction) and batch size 32 for high throughput (higher P95). We’ll report P50/P95 latency and tokens/$ for each.

Evaluation plan (what Redwood will deliver):
1) Traffic shaping & sims (5 business days) — run the sample through our simulator and generate per-policy tokens/$ sensitivity curves. Deliverable: tokens-per-USD curves + a recommended pilot config.
2) Small-scale pilot (2 weeks) — run with live traffic on a dedicated small pool to validate sims and measure real cache hit / batching latencies. Deliverable: pilot readout + delta vs sims.
3) Gate decision (MAP checkpoint) — we produce a pass/fail on units/$ with signoff options (green: within 10% of sims; amber: 10–25% discrepancy + mitigation plan; red: >25% discrepancy).

Proposed mutual owners & tentative dates (we can move earlier if you need):
- Lukas (Redwood) — delivery of sim curves: 2027-05-11
- Karthik (Redwood infra) — pilot config + SLO definition: 2027-05-13
- Medicorps (Samir / Procurement) — procurement readiness decision: 2027-05-28

Initial assumptions we’ll use (editable in workbook):
- Token unit cost (baseline hosted): $0.0009 per token (decoder); we’ll provide a dedicated-reserved estimate too.
- Model footprint: 7B dense baseline for sims; quantized variants discussed as uplift.
- Prefetch cost: models the additional tokens consumed to warm prefixes (we’ll show tokens consumed per warm event).

Notes / risks:
- If your traffic has heavy long conversations (>2k tokens/session) batching effects change — we’ll flag those.
- Procurement typically asks for committed capacity pricing; we’ll provide an annual vs monthly split in the workbook.

Action items (short):
- Samir: confirm the sample is representative (click/engagement cohort) and share any target throughput windows (peak qps) — due EOD 2027-05-06
- Karthik: validate pilot infra template and share expected P95 overhead by 2027-05-06
- Lukas: deliver sim curves by 2027-05-11 (I’ll attach the workbook now)

(attachment: lukas_map_draft_v1.xlsx - workbook; inference-sim-results.pdf - quick sim snapshots)

— Lukas
Lukas Meyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - unit-econ sensitivity + prefetch/batching Qs

Quick technical clarifications from infra so the sims match reality: 

1) Batching tradeoffs (we’ll report latency at these points):
   - batch=1: throughput low, per-token overhead minimal — baseline token latency (decoder path)
   - batch=8: ~1.6x tokens/sec improvement vs batch=1, P95 adds ~10–25ms depending on kernel warming
   - batch=32: ~3.8x tokens/sec improvement vs batch=1, P95 adds ~40–120ms in small pools; better in large pre-warmed pools

2) Prefetch cost modeling:
   - Prefetch warms KV cache by sending a ~50–120 token warm request per session; if hit ratio is 60% we amortize that cost across follow-up requests; effective tokens added = warm_tokens * (1 - amortization_factor) in sim.

3) Token unit cost note: the $0.0009 baseline is for hosted decoder tokens. For dedicated reserved pools we’ll model an effective token cost that includes reserved GPU amortization and will present both per-request and blended rates.

Small sensitivity table we’ll include in sim workbook (example numbers):
   - Profile A (250 t/s): tokens/$ (no cache) = 1,111; tokens/$ (60% cache) = 1,780
   - Profile B (850 t/s): tokens/$ (no cache) = 3,780; tokens/$ (60% cache) = 5,950

Hannah — I think we should flag quantized model variants as an optional scenario (7B q4 -> ~20–40% token-cost improvement in sim).

I’ll prep an infra appendix for the workbook by EOD 2027-05-06 with the exact latency curves we used.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
